newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Apple stands still.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Apple stands still.

text.p: Shares in Apple Computer Inc barely moved in after-hours trade as the company reported a third quarter loss of $0.44 per share, traders said Wednedsay.
The troubled personal computer maker, forced to layoff a quarter of its workforce earlier in the year, traded at 16-1/2 after the bell, up a hair from an unofficial close of 16-7/16.
VERITAS Software Corp, meanwhile, gained 3/4, rising to 61 from a 60-1/4 close after announcing a three-for-two stock split.
VERITAS, which makes storage management products, also reported second quarter proforma fully-taxed earnings of $0.22 per share, compared with $0.13 per share for the year-ago period.
Also after the bell, AT&T's stock price dipped slightly on news of a management shakeup.
Dealers said the long distance phone service fell to 36 from an unofficial close of 36-5/16 after the bell.

Just minutes before the U.S. market close, AT&T announced that its president had resigned following a decision not to elevate him to chief executive. In last-minute regular-hours trade the company's stock added about a point.
Traders said other stocks generally traded in line with their closing prices as earnings releases dominated after-hours news.
The session followed a landmark day for the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which burst through the 8,000 mark, finishing up 63 points.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one volume rose to 112,600 from 40,400 the previous day. Session two volume was 6,850,000, up from 629,189.
